textbookText: From the solution of the mixture of copper sulphate and common salt, copper hydroxide is precipitated out by the addition of excess of sodium hydroxide solution. Copper hydroxide is decomposed into black oxide of copper (i.e., cupric oxide) under the action of heat. The black oxide of copper is treated with dilute sulphuric acid. Thus obtained copper sulphate solution is subjected to crystallization to obtain blue vibiol crystals. ----....--..---.-.--+ cu (OH)2 + NaS04 cuS04 + NaOH bluish white ppt Cuo (s) + H2S04 (aq) ----——cuS04 (aq) + H20 (1) crystallization CuS04 (aq) CuS04 5H20 blue vitriol crystals The copper sulphate can be obtained in pure state by washing black oxide of copper with distilled water several times. The residue-washed water is treated with AgN03 solution and BaC12 solution separately.
Presence of chloride and sulphate ions is indicated by formation of a white precipitate with AgN03 and BaC12 solutions respectively.

PROCESS
Glass rod Liquid Filter paper Filtrate Figure 2.16: Filtration Take the given mixture of copper sulphate and sodium chloride in a beaker. Add water to dissolve it.
Add dilute NaOH to it. A bluish white precipitate is seen. Allow the solution to stand for some time.
To ensure the complete conversion of copper sulphate into copper hydroxide, add few drops of dilute NaOH to the supernatant liquid• If a fresh precipitate is seen, add few more drops of dilute NaOH.
Check for the completeness of precipitation as before. When no more fresh precipitate is seen, stop adding sodium hydroxide solution.
Heat the mixture in the beaker. Black oxide of copper is formed.
When the mixture turns completely black, filter the mixture solution in the beaker.
Separation of Mixtures Wash the residue in the filter paper (i.e. black oxide of copper) with distilled water to make it free from chloride ion (NaCl solution) and sulphate ion (Na2S04 solution).
After washing 2-3 times, treat the precipitate-washed water coming out from the stem of the funnel with few drops of AgN03 solution.
Similarly, treat it with few drops of BaC12 solution in another test tube.

If a white precipitate is formed with AgN03 solution, this indicates the presence of chloride ion in the residue. Similarly, formation of a white precipitate with BaC12 solution indicates the presence of sulphate ion in the residue.
10. If a ppt is formed in any of the test tubes, wash the residue again and

perform the tests in no. (8) again. II. If no ppt is seen in both the test tubes, then make a hole in the filter paper and vyash down the residue in a porcelain basin with a minimum quantity of water with the help of a wash bottle.
12. Decant the black oxide of copper and drain out water as maximum
as possible (there should not be any loss of copper oxide).
13. Dissolve the cupric oxide in minimum quantity of dilute sulphuric
acid stirring with the help of a glass rod. Blue copper sulphate solution is formed.
14. The solution is filtered. The filtrate taken in a basin is heated upto the
crystallization point by placing it over the sand bath. Stir the evaporated solution to avoid the crust formation.

The crystallization point is ascertained by introducing few drops of the evaporated solution with the help of a glass rod on the outer wall of the test tube which is filled with cold water, Blue crystals are seen on the wall of the test tube when the solution attains the crystallization point. As soon as the solution attains the crystallization point, avoid heating.
Float the porcelain basin on water taken in a beaker. The blue crystals of copper sulphate separate out slowly on cooling.
Drain off the mother liquor after complete separation of the blue crystals.
Collect all the crystals on a filter paper without disturbing the shape of the crystals.
Finally, dry the crystals of blue vitriol in the folds of the filter paper or in air.
